answer_text:
Here is a comprehensive **7-Day China Itinerary** following the classic "Golden Triangle" route — **Beijing → Xi'an → Chengdu → Shanghai** — ideal for first-time visitors who want a perfect mix of history, culture, nature, and modernity!

---

## 🇨🇳 7-Day China Trip: Beijing, Xi'an, Chengdu & Shanghai

---

### 🗓️ Day 1 — Arrival in Beijing

Welcome to Beijing! Once you land, you're right in the middle of China's rich history. Take the Airport Express train to the city center — it's a better option than taxis during rush hour.

- Check into your hotel and freshen up.
- Spend your evening walking through the vibrant **Dongcheng district**.
- Try **Peking duck** for dinner, one of Beijing's most iconic dishes.

> 💡 **Tip:** Get WeChat and a VPN before you arrive, since most Western apps don't work in China.

---

### 🗓️ Day 2 — Beijing: Tiananmen Square, Forbidden City & Hutongs

Beijing is home to many big-ticket attractions: the Forbidden City, the Great Wall, Tiananmen Square, the Summer Palace, and more.

- Start your day at **Tiananmen Square** around 7:30 AM before the crowds arrive, then head to **Jingshan Park** for excellent views of the Forbidden City.
- Among China's imperial sights, none can compare in size, grandeur, or mystique to the **Forbidden City**. Built between 1406 and 1420, this sprawling palace was off-limits for 500 years.
- In the afternoon, explore the traditional **hutongs** around Nanluoguxiang. Wear good walking shoes — you'll walk 5–6 miles on uneven ground.

> 💡 **Tip:** Security around Tiananmen Square is tightly controlled; expect to show your passport at multiple checkpoints. Advance reservations must be made via WeChat.

---

### 🗓️ Day 3 — Beijing: The Great Wall & Ming Tombs

- Visit the **Mutianyu section** of the Great Wall — it's less busy than Badaling and the views are better. Take the early bus to get more time at the wall.
- Among the wall's sections, **Jinshanling** has the most beautiful scenery for hiking, while **Mutianyu** has densely spaced watchtowers and is easier to climb, making it suitable for families.
- Afternoon: Visit the **Ming Tombs**.
- At night, take the **overnight train to Xi'an**. Book a top bunk if you want more privacy at a lower price.

---

### 🗓️ Day 4 — Xi'an: Terracotta Warriors & City Wall

- Start your day with a visit to the world-famous **Terracotta Warriors**, thousands of life-sized clay soldiers that have been standing guard for over 2,000 years — truly one of China's greatest historical treasures.
- The Terracotta Army has been laid underground for more than 2,000 years. However, in 1974, farmers digging a well uncovered one of the greatest archaeological sites in the world. In 1987 it became a World Cultural Heritage site.
- In the afternoon, **ride a bike along the ancient Xi'an City Wall**, one of the best-preserved city walls in China.
- Evening: Explore the vibrant **Muslim Quarter** for street food and culture.

> 💡 **Tip:** Take bus 914 from the station to the Terracotta Warriors for ¥7 instead of paying for expensive transfers.

---

### 🗓️ Day 5 — Xi'an to Chengdu: Pandas & Jinli Street

- Visit the historic **Giant Wild Goose Pagoda** before departing Xi'an.
- Head to **Chengdu** by flight or high-speed train. Once you arrive, slow things down with a walk along **Jinli Ancient Street** — full of glowing lanterns, traditional architecture, and delicious Sichuan snacks. It's the perfect place to get a feel for Chengdu's laid-back vibe.

---

### 🗓️ Day 6 — Chengdu: Giant Pandas & Local Life

- Get to the **Giant Panda Breeding Center** when it opens at 7:30 AM to see the pandas eat breakfast. Later, visit **People's Park** to watch locals play mahjong and practice tai chi. Finish your day in the **Kuanzhai Xiangzi alleys** where old meets new.
- With its charming teahouses, lively nightlife, and fiery **Sichuan food**, Chengdu is one of China's most popular cities for travelers.
- Evening: Fly or take a high-speed train to **Shanghai**.

---

### 🗓️ Day 7 — Shanghai: The Bund, Yu Garden & Farewell

- Stroll along **The Bund** to admire the striking skyline across the river. Then explore the classical beauty of **Yu Garden** and its bustling surrounding market.
- Visit the **Shanghai Tower**, China's tallest building, offering panoramic views of the city.
- Pop into the **Old Town Bazaar** for souvenir shopping — local teas, silk scarves, hand fans, and calligraphy sets. For lunch, don't miss the famous **Xiao Long Bao** (soup dumplings) at the original Nanxiang restaurant nearby.
- Head to the airport for departure.

---

## 🧳 Essential Travel Tips

- **Best Time to Visit:** Spring (April–May) and autumn (September–October) offer the most comfortable weather nationwide.
- **Getting Around:** China's high-speed rail network is a great option for traveling between cities — bullet trains are fast, efficient, and often more convenient than flying for mid-range distances. Major cities like Beijing, Shanghai, and Xi'an are well connected.
- **Payments:** Cash is fading fast — WeChat Pay and Alipay are widely used. Tourists can now link international cards through special versions of these apps.
- **Language:** Mandarin Chinese is the official language, though English is increasingly common in tourist areas. Translation apps prove invaluable for navigation and communication.
- **Visa:** China currently offers visa-free entry
